- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward in next 5–7 days — apply a “lag correction” by adding 1–2% back to forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model tends to overestimate near-term price — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods — if 3–5 day average of sentiment is negative, forecast should be closer to 10–15 day moving average of price.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates downward trends — increase forecast by 3–7% if sentiment is consistently negative over last 7–10 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model may lag in recognizing reversal — add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment shift.
